description: A composite figure mixing nanoindentation mechanical data with secondary-electron (SE) micrographs for the hardest aging condition of three Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels. (a) is in fact three separate nanoindentation load-displacement plots, each tagged in a yellow box as 15Al, 17Al and 19Al; the y-axis is Load (mN) (ticks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and up to 10 in the 17Al and 19Al plots) and the x-axis is Displacement (nm) from 0 to 250. Every plot overlays many loading/unloading curves rising to about 8-9 mN near 200-220 nm displacement and unloading to residual displacements around 110-140 nm. Printed inside each panel is H_Ave = 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa (15Al), 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa (17Al) and 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa (19Al). (b) shows three SE micrographs of polished surfaces carrying 4 × 4 indentation arrays, each indent annotated with its hardness in GPa and a 2 µm scale bar; 15Al and 17Al surfaces look blocky/lamellar while 19Al shows a finer needle-like structure. The spread of indentation values widens from 15Al to 19Al. The caption also refers to a panel (c), SE images with corresponding EDS elemental mapping, which is not present in the supplied image.

observations.observation: Panel (a) comprises three separate nanoindentation load-displacement plots, labelled 15Al, 17Al and 19Al in yellow boxes, with Load (mN) versus Displacement (nm) axes spanning 0-250 nm on the x-axis.
Each load-displacement plot overlays many individual load/unload curves that reach about 8-9 mN at roughly 200-220 nm displacement and unload to residual displacements of roughly 110-140 nm.
Printed average nanohardness values inside the panels are H_Ave = 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa for 15Al, 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa for 17Al and 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa for 19Al.
Panel (b) contains three SE micrographs of polished surfaces, each with a 4 × 4 indentation array annotated with individual hardness values in GPa and a 2 µm scale bar.
In panel (b) the 15Al indent values span 10.9-12.4 GPa, the 17Al values 10.2-12.3 GPa, and the 19Al values 8.0-12.9 GPa, so the scatter of individual indentations widens with increasing Al content.
The 19Al SE micrograph shows a distinctly finer needle-like/lath microstructure, whereas the 15Al and 17Al surfaces appear coarser and blocky/lamellar.
The samples shown are 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h, 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h, and 19Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 10 h.
The caption states that panel (c) shows SE images with corresponding EDS elemental mapping of the indentations; no such panel is present in the supplied image.

The peak Vickers hardness values for the 15Al, 17Al and 19Al alloys were 965.6 HV, 924.9 HV and 917.8 HV respectively, and both peak Vickers hardness and micro-hardness decreased with increasing Al content.
The average nanohardness measured by nanoindentation was 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa (15Al), 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa (17Al) and 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa (19Al), matching the values printed in Fig. 13(a).
The intrinsic hardness of β-Mn for 15Al, 17Al and 19Al was 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa, 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa and 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa respectively, i.e. slightly increasing with Al content, while overall hardness decreased.
The citation attributes the variation in micro-hardness across areas in Fig. 13(b) to the presence of FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases between the β-Mn, whose intrinsic hardness is lower than that of β-Mn.

The citation states that indentations not contacting the FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases were used to derive the intrinsic hardness of β-Mn, and that the increased error in micro-hardness with Al content reflects a larger content of those precipitates.

The overall hardness decrease with increasing Al content is explained by the growing volume fraction of FCC Cu-rich and BCC precipitates at the β-Mn interfaces, reducing the absolute volume fraction of β-Mn.

subfigures.description: Nanoindentation load-displacement plot for the 15Al alloy (yellow label box). Axes: Load (mN) 0-~9 vs Displacement (nm) 0-250; many overlapping load/unload curves peak near 8 mN at ~200 nm with residual displacement ~110-130 nm. Printed annotation: H_Ave = 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa.
Nanoindentation load-displacement plot for the 17Al alloy. Load axis 0-10 mN, displacement 0-250 nm; curve families peak near 8-9 mN at ~210 nm. Printed annotation: H_Ave = 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa.

Nanoindentation load-displacement plot for the 19Al alloy. Load axis 0-10 mN, displacement 0-250 nm; the loading and unloading branches are visibly more scattered/spread than in 15Al and 17Al. Printed annotation: H_Ave = 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa.

SE micrograph of a polished 15Al surface with a 4 × 4 array of indentations, each labelled with its hardness in GPa (11.1, 12.3, 11.9, 12.2 / 11.4, 12.1, 12.1, 10.9 / 12.4, 11.6, 11.4, 11.5 / 11.9, 11.5, 12.0, 11.5 GPa). Scale bar 2 µm.

SE micrograph of a polished 17Al surface with a 4 × 4 indentation array labelled in GPa (11.6, 11.1, 10.2, 10.7 / 12.1, 10.8, 10.6, 11.1 / 11.0, 10.6, 10.5, 11.3 / 11.1, 12.3, 11.4, 10.9 GPa). Scale bar 2 µm.

SE micrograph of a polished 19Al surface with a 4 × 4 indentation array labelled in GPa (10.2, 12.2, 12.9, 9.6 / 8.5, 11.0, 10.7, 10.5 / 11.9, 8.8, 10.4, 8.0 / 10.2, 9.7, 9.8, 11.1 GPa); the surface shows a fine needle-like/lath texture. Scale bar 2 µm.
